items.headline: The valuation read is being pulled by sentiment
items.detail: The composite sits at the 21th percentile, but the sentiment axis is at 89 while the rest average 28 — the one dimension running hot.
items.framing: Everything is cheap except sentiment, which reads 89/100. That divergence is the story — it's how the exchange-flow build-up first became visible.
items.checkable: Each axis is a percentile of its own history; published weights on the Methods page.

items.headline: The base is sitting tighter than usual
items.detail: Liveliness 0.610 is 2.9σ down vs its month. Rising = old coins moving (distribution/rotation); falling = holders sitting still (accumulation).
items.framing: Coins are sitting tighter — liveliness fell. The base is holding, dormancy deepening.
items.checkable: Coin-days-destroyed vs coin-days-stored from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: -80% below its all-time high
items.detail: Deepest drawdown on record was -95%; it has made new highs after every prior one so far.
items.framing: Deep drawdowns are the toll — it's paid them before (no recovery promise).
items.note: It's deep and unrecovered NOW; don't imply it always recovers.

items.headline: SPX's MVRV 0.92 = 10th percentile of Bitcoin's history
items.detail: SPX's MVRV of 0.92 sits at the 10th percentile of Bitcoin's entire MVRV history — as cheap as BTC's generational bottoms.
items.framing: MVRV is unitless, so it's comparable: SPX today is at BTC's 10th percentile. BTC was only this cheap at major bottoms.
items.note: A position on BTC's map, not a date-match forecast.

items.headline: -81% below its long-run trend (Fire Sale band)
items.detail: Fair value for its age is $2.37; price sits -81% under it.
items.framing: Where today sits in the long power-law arc.

items.headline: 80% of all-time holders are gone — 92% of today's never sold to zero
items.detail: Of 26,942 wallets that ever held ≥5k SPX, 5,346 remain (80% churned). Yet 92% of CURRENT holders have never once sold to zero — survivorship.
items.framing: Enormous all-time churn, but the survivors are diamond-handed. The honest "who's still here" read.
items.note: Right-censoring: recent cohorts read high. "Gone" = fell below the 5k bar.

items.headline: Smart money still net-selling (-15.1% over 12w)
items.detail: The 10-wallet cohort of proven top-timers (ROI ≥5×, still holding) holds 6.96M SPX. 4w -13.2% · 12w -15.1% · 26w -22.5%.
items.framing: Smart money hasn't started buying yet (-15.1% in 12w). Honest "not the bottom signal yet" read.
items.checkable: A recomputed cohort of wallets with realized ROI ≥5× that still hold ≥50k SPX; net flow of their combined balance.

items.headline: 1 new proven top-timer in 90 days
items.detail: Wallet(s) that just crossed the ROI+capital bar by selling a top at profit — a burst means distribution is starting.
items.framing: 1 wallet(s) newly qualified as smart money in 90d (sold a top at ≥5× ROI). Low count = quiet market; a spike is the tell.
items.checkable: First crossing of the ROI+capital bar per wallet, from the sale history.

items.detail: 0x446b…27ba accumulated over the window, one of 3 whales net-buying.
items.framing: A large wallet accumulated 700k SPX in 7 days. Real, checkable buying by a big holder.

items.detail: 0xb744…337d is the biggest net buyer of Project AEON over 30 days — 2.3 ETH ($6,230), well clear of the field.

items.headline: NUPL -0.09 — capitulation
items.detail: Net unrealised profit/loss is -0.09 (from MVRV 0.92) — the market sits in the capitulation zone.
items.framing: Aggregate holder profitability. Below zero = the crowd is underwater, historically an accumulation zone.
items.note: A position read, not a signal.

items.headline: -1.2σ below its trend vs the alt market
items.detail: SPX ÷ the alt sector (ex-BTC/ETH/stables), detrended, sits 1.2σ below its own trend — cheap vs alts.
items.framing: Relative value vs the whole alt sector — -1.2σ cheap. SPX structurally outperforms alts, so this is deviation from ITS trend, not parity.
items.note: A relative-value position, not a signal.

items.headline: A 1.77M-SPX holder moved everything to a new wallet of its own
items.detail: 2026-09-26 (5d ago). A test send, a test sent back, then the whole balance — the coins keep their age and cost, so it is not a sale and books no profit or loss.
items.framing: A 1.77M SPX position changed wallets on 2026-09-26: same holder, new address. Say "moved to a new wallet", never "sold" or "exited".
items.checkable: The handshake (small send, small send back, then the balance) is in the raw transfer history; both wallets are linked below.

items.headline: 177× at this age — vs Ethereum's 75×
items.detail: At the same age since launch (~3yr), SPX6900 is 177× vs Ethereum's 75× at the same point in its life.
items.framing: History rhymes: at this age SPX is 177×, Ethereum was 75×. A same-age comparison, not a forecast.
items.note: Both indexed to their own launch; close-based.

items.headline: 236,588 holders across 3 chains
items.detail: ETH 49,125 · Base 114,129 · Solana 73,334 = 236,588 wallets, +2.9% in ~30d. Base leads on headcount, ETH on value.
items.framing: The real reach: 236,588 wallets across three chains — most people on Base/Solana, most value on ETH.
items.note: Wallets, not people; Base/Solana are bridged.

items.note: Coin age from the FIFO reconstruction.

items.headline: +11% since the last Fire Sale low (2026-09-29)

items.framing: Every capitulation-band low has rallied off it.
items.note: Pattern, not a promise; the chart shows the first 90 days.

items.headline: SOPR 0.963 — coins moving at a loss
items.detail: Spent-output profit ratio is 0.963: coins that moved on-chain realised a loss on average. Sustained <1 = capitulation, >1 = profit-taking.
items.framing: On-chain realised behaviour — loss-realisation (SOPR 0.963).
items.note: Only coins that MOVED; a behaviour read, not a signal.

items.headline: 1.46M SPX left in a day
items.detail: 2026-09-30: 61 wallets dropped below the 5k bar with 1.46M SPX, 2.5σ above the usual churn — 52% in profit (profit-taking).
items.framing: A profit-taking exit wave — 61 wallets banked 1.46M SPX and stepped down. Holders selling strength, not fear; the honest hook is WHO takes profit and when.
items.checkable: Wallets whose balance fell below the 5k residency bar that day, split by exit vs entry price.
